scope: short-duration mild vomiting or diarrhea in an alert person who can take small sips; not for infants, frail adults, or people with concerning red flags
patterns: I have mild diarrhea and want to stay hydrated
what should I drink after vomiting
my child vomited once but is acting normally
toddler has diarrhea but is still drinking
what can I do at home for mild vomiting
cannot eat much after being sick but can sip water
should I use oral rehydration after diarrhea
response: Focus on fluids rather than forcing food. Offer small, frequent sips. An oral rehydration solution can help replace fluid and salts, especially for children, and should be prepared according to its label. If vomiting happens after a drink, pause briefly and try smaller sips.
red_flags: blood in vomit or stool, or green vomit
signs of dehydration or inability to keep any fluids down
infant under 6 months with any diarrhea or vomiting
symptoms lasting more than a couple of days or clearly worsening
pregnancy, chronic illness, or other higher-risk situation
